+import typing
+
+from sqlalchemy.engine.row import Row, RowMapping
+

+class Record:
+    """
+    Wraps a SQLAlchemy ``Row`` to provide both mapping and sequence access.
+
+    SQLAlchemy 2.x ``Row`` objects only support positional access via
+    ``__getitem__``; column access by name requires using the ``._mapping``
+    attribute.  This wrapper restores the behaviour that ``databases`` has
+    historically exposed, where ``row["column"]`` and ``row[0]`` both work,
+    and records behave like mappings when passed to ``dict()``.
+    """
+
+    __slots__ = ("_row",)
+
+    def __init__(self, row: Row) -> None:
+        object.__setattr__(self, "_row", row)
+
+    @property
+    def _mapping(self) -> RowMapping:
+        return self._row._mapping
+
+    def __getitem__(self, key: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:
+        if isinstance(key, int):
+            return self._row[key]
+        return self._mapping[key]
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> typing.Iterator[str]:
+        return iter(self._mapping.keys())
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._row)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> typing.Any:
+        return getattr(self._row, name)
+
+    def keys(self) -> typing.Iterable[str]:
+        return self._mapping.keys()
+
+    def values(self) -> typing.Iterable[typing.Any]:
+        return self._mapping.values()
+
+    def items(self) -> typing.Iterable[typing.Tuple[str, typing.Any]]:
+        return self._mapping.items()
